hypotheses.claim: Using QueueDepth (not EffectiveLoad) for the pile-on penalty catches rapid queue buildup faster since QueueDepth is the most responsive signal
hypotheses.mechanism: QueueDepth reflects waiting requests directly; BatchSize and PendingRequests add noise; QueueDepth-based penalty reacts faster to burst arrivals

hypotheses.claim: Increasing session affinity weight to 0.92 for long sessions (inputLen>=256) and adding FreeKVBlocks tiebreaker improves multiturn
hypotheses.mechanism: Longer sessions have more KV state to recompute on miss; stronger affinity plus memory-aware tiebreaking reduces recomputation

hypotheses.claim: Adding QueueDepth-specific penalty on top of EffectiveLoad penalty catches pile-on faster in load_spikes, reducing load_spikes_e2e_ms
hypotheses.mechanism: QueueDepth reflects actual waiting requests; when prefix-affinity piles onto one instance, QueueDepth spikes before EffectiveLoad fully reflects it; extra QueueDepth penalty redirects faster

hypotheses.claim: Reducing prefix weight for non-session interactive requests when load spread is high prevents dominant-prefix hot-spotting
hypotheses.mechanism: In load_spikes, one prefix group dominates; non-session requests in that group don't need sticky routing; reducing w0 when maxLoad-minLoad>3 spreads traffic

hypotheses.claim: Preserving session override and CacheHitRate bonus maintains multiturn performance while new penalties improve other workloads
hypotheses.mechanism: Session requests bypass the load-spread w0 reduction; CacheHitRate tiebreaker steers sessions to warm instances
